To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

We present a novel technique that can automatically identify nodes in an anonymized social network using a small set of training examples and that it can be used to evaluate the efficacy of black-box anonymization schemes.

1) the technique is effective at re-identifying social network nodes in anonymized datasets; 2) the technique can be used to evaluate the effectiveness of anonymization schemes; 3) the technique can re-identify social network nodes even in the absence of ground-truth data; 4) the technique can detect the anonymization scheme in use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a tool to help researchers and developers to understand and improve anonymization techniques for social graphs.
the development of a technique to re-identify nodes from anonymized graphs.
the problem of evaluating and comparing anonymization strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the technique is very effective in identifying nodes in one social graph when trained with samples from another social network.
this technique provides a useful way to evaluate anonymization techniques and can be used to de-anonymize social networks.
our approach provides a generic and automated method to evaluate anonymization schemes, and it is effective even when small numbers of samples and small false positive rates can be tolerated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a technique which is capable of re-identifying a significant number of nodes in anonymized graphs.
we present a generic and efficient approach to de-anonymizing social networks.
the proposed technique is generic and automated and is able to re-identify nodes even in large anonymized social networks with high accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to automatically detect and re-identify nodes across disparate anonymized social networks.
it is possible to quickly and automatically evaluate the performance of anonymization schemes without having to understand their internal workings.
anonymization of social graphs is not as robust as is often claimed.
